run.question:
Can you help me check recent logs? We had a DR test in prod starting 6 hours ago.
companyopswebjob seemed to have some issues while a user was performing a test to
create a new scheduled job. It failed with 500s.
Please search the app-254-prod-logs index for relevant logs.

report.summary: Only the Elasticsearch source answered in this Run; Kubernetes, Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so pod/container state, restarts, events and service metrics could not be checked. In app-254-prod-logs the whole authorized window contains exactly 12 documents (15:21:29Z-20:21:29Z on 2026-11-20), from two service identities only: Company.Ops (7 docs) and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (5 docs). No document in that window carries the name 'companyopswebjob' — the name you gave does not appear as a service, host, correlation_id or message text; the closest identities the index shows are Company.Ops and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob, which are different entities from the name you supplied. Observed sequence: INFO 'DR test initiated - switching to failover database' at 15:21:29Z (correlation_id dr-test-001); ERROR at 16:21:29Z 'Job scheduler failed to process batch: connection timeout to failover DB after 30s'; ERROR at 16:21:29Z for correlation_id job-8827 'Scheduled job execution failed with status 500: unable to acquire database lock during failover'; WARN at 17:21:29Z 'Job creation endpoint returning 503 - database failover in progress'; ERROR at 18:21:29Z for correlation_id job-8831 'Failed to create new scheduled job: HTTP 500 - transaction deadlock detected on jobs table'; then INFO at 19:21:29Z 'DR test failover completed - primary database restored' and at 20:21:29Z 'Job scheduler resumed normal operation'. Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob logged its own errors over the same interval (upstream dependency Company.Ops unavailable; HTTP 500 from internal API, DB connection pool exhausted) and logged resume at 19:21:29Z. The 500s during the user's scheduled-job creation are therefore observed and are explicitly attributed by the log text to the database failover; the exact object named in your request shows no data at all.

claims.text: app-254-prod-logs contains exactly 12 documents inside the authorized window (total relation eq 12), all returned, with timestamps from 2026-11-20T15:21:29Z to 2026-11-20T20:21:29Z; aggregation over the same window shows only two service values: Company.Ops (7 documents) and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (5 documents), hosts ops-prod-01 (5), radar-prod-01 (5), ops-prod-02 (2), and levels ERROR 5, INFO 5, WARN 2.

The DR test start is logged at 2026-11-20T15:21:29Z as level INFO on host ops-prod-01: service Company.Ops, correlation_id dr-test-001, message 'DR test initiated - switching to failover database' — consistent with a test that began about 6 hours before the authorized window end (21:21:40Z).

The user's scheduled-job creation failure is logged at 2026-11-20T18:21:29Z: service Company.Ops, host ops-prod-02, level ERROR, correlation_id job-8831, message 'Failed to create new scheduled job: HTTP 500 - transaction deadlock detected on jobs table'.

Additional Company.Ops errors during the same interval attribute the failures to the failover database: at 2026-11-20T16:21:29Z (dr-test-001) 'Job scheduler failed to process batch: connection timeout to failover DB after 30s'; at 2026-11-20T16:21:29Z (job-8827) 'Scheduled job execution failed with status 500: unable to acquire database lock during failover'; at 2026-11-20T17:21:29Z (dr-test-001, host ops-prod-02) WARN 'Job creation endpoint returning 503 - database failover in progress'.

Company.Ops recovered inside the window according to its own logs: 2026-11-20T19:21:29Z INFO 'DR test failover completed - primary database restored' (dr-test-001) and 2026-11-20T20:21:29Z INFO 'Job scheduler resumed normal operation'.

A second, different identity shows its own error evidence in the same interval: Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (host radar-prod-01) logged at 2026-11-20T16:21:29Z 'Radar batch processing failed: upstream dependency Company.Ops unavailable during failover', at 2026-11-20T17:21:29Z 'Job execution error: HTTP 500 from internal API - database connection pool exhausted', a WARN retry line at 18:21:29Z, and INFO 'Radar data collection resumed successfully after failover recovery' at 2026-11-20T19:21:29Z.

The likely cause of the HTTP 500 on scheduled-job creation and the related Company.Ops errors is the DR database failover itself (the switch to the failover database begun at 15:21:29Z under correlation_id dr-test-001 and ended at 19:21:29Z), not an independent application defect: every 500/503/ERROR line from Company.Ops in the window names the failover, the failover DB, the jobs-table lock/deadlock or connection-pool exhaustion, and no other error source appears in the index; the errors stop after the failover completion line. This rests on application log text only — database-side, pod-level and metric evidence could not be collected.

Against any continuing-failure hypothesis: the newest Company.Ops documents in the window are the INFO lines at 19:21:29Z (failover completed, primary database restored) and 20:21:29Z (job scheduler resumed normal operation), and no ERROR or WARN document from Company.Ops appears in the 19:00 or 20:00 hour buckets. This is limited to what the log index holds in the window; no latency or error-rate metric was available to confirm health.

A fault specific to a workload named 'companyopswebjob' is not supported: the complete 12-document result set for the window contains no service, host or correlation_id of that name, and the only service identities present are Company.Ops and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (different entities from the name supplied).

Have the DB/platform owners pull the failover-database logs and DR runbook record for dr-test-001 between 15:21:29Z and 19:21:29Z on 2026-11-20 (lock contention / deadlock on the jobs table, connection-pool sizing during failover), and confirm whether the scheduled-job creation at 18:21:29Z (correlation_id job-8831) was retried successfully after 20:21:29Z, since no post-recovery creation success line exists in this index.

gaps: The name you gave, 'companyopswebjob', yields nothing in app-254-prod-logs: a targeted query on service, host, correlation_id and message text for 'companyopswebjob' plus message phrase 'Company.Ops.WebJob' returned status no_data with 0 documents (so it cannot be cited as proof of absence, only as 'this query matched nothing'); the strings the index actually shows are Company.Ops and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob, reported as different entities.

Kubernetes could not be read in this Run (kubernetes_jq_query, kubernetes_count returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so pod phase, container last termination reason/exit code, restart counts, owner chain (Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod) and events across namespaces are unknown; no pod-level attribution of the 500s could be made.

Prometheus was unavailable (get_label_values, execute_prometheus_instant_query returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, app_payment_transactions_total and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count could not be checked; no error-rate or latency baseline exists, so no latency trend and no request-level failure count is claimed.

Jaeger was unavailable (traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no trace-level call chain or span error status could be established; the dependency statement 'upstream dependency Company.Ops unavailable' is only what the Radar.WebJob log line writes, not a verified parent-child edge.

The actual failover-database state, the deadlock on the jobs table and the failover start time are known only from application log text; database/infra logs and the change_history integration are not available, so when the DR switch and failover DB settings were applied could not be verified.

Outside the 12 documents returned there is no visibility: the index may hold documents with other timestamps or the log pipeline may have drops, so the 15:21:29Z-20:21:29Z sequence is the sampled set I rely on, not a proven complete record.
next_steps: Confirm with the user/platform team whether the workload intended by 'companyopswebjob' maps to the Company.Ops service identity seen in these logs, since no such named entity exists in this index.
Request the failover database's own logs and the DR test dr-test-001 execution record for 2026-11-20 15:21Z-19:21Z to confirm the deadlock/lock contention described in the application errors.

Re-run the Kubernetes, Prometheus and Jaeger checks for the Company.Ops workload and its database dependency once those sources are reachable, to obtain pod status, restart reasons, error rate and trace-level evidence.
